To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
auditory training targeted to improve perceptually-based language and learning skills can alter the pre-conscious neural encoding of speech by improving neural synchronicity in the human brain.

(1) Auditory training can alter the encoding of speech in the human brain; (2) Auditory training improves neural encoding in the brainstem; (3) Neural encoding improvements are associated with perceptual, academic and cognitive improvements; (4) Neural encoding improvements in the brainstem are associated with improvements in cortical physiology; (5) Neural encoding improvements occur in the brainstem in a frequency-specific manner; (6) Neural encoding improvements can be measured with the brainstem response; and
auditory training can alter neural encoding of speech in the human brain, and that these changes are related to changes in brainstem physiology and perceptual and cognitive measures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the plasticity of the human auditory brainstem.
the development of a new paradigm for remediation of auditory and speech deficits in children and adults with learning impairments.
the development of the human brain, and the plasticity of the neural system in response to training.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brainstem response timing changes in trained children were related to improvements in cortical processing of the acoustic structure of speech.

training improved brainstem neural synchrony and this improvement was associated with changes in cortical auditory function, as well as improved perceptual, academic and cognitive measures in children with learning disabilities.

the auditory training program improved the neural encoding of speech in the auditory brain, and this improvement was related to improvements in cortical physiology and perceptual, academic and cognitive measures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the auditory brainstem response (ABR) is a reliable and sensitive measure of auditory function, which can be used to evaluate the efficacy of auditory training.
auditory training can improve the preconscious neural processing of speech in children with learning problems, which in turn is related to changes in perceptual, cognitive, and academic abilities.
auditory training targeted to perceptual learning problems can alter neural encoding of the auditory signal in the human brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
auditory training can change the brainstem encoding of complex sounds.
auditory training can alter preconscious auditory encoding, and that these changes in neural timing are correlated with changes in cortical physiology.
the auditory brainstem is a dynamic and plastic structure, which is capable of adapting to auditory training.
